Where the gene lists come from

These lists map measured human gene RNA to named anatomical regions. They do not locate individual protein molecules, establish protein abundance in a cortical parcel, or identify a gene's exclusive location. BigBrain geometry and expression measurements come from different specimens.

Measurements and anatomical precision

  • Human Protein Atlas (HPA) version 25.1, Ensembl 109, retrieved 28 October 2026. The human brain table contains 193 sampled areas; a separate prefrontal study contains 20 areas. The interface names the source study for each parcel. Values from these studies are not pooled.
  • A gene is listed as detected when at least one corresponding source area has nTPM ≥ 1, using the HPA detection convention. The displayed value is the maximum across the listed source-area summaries. Individual values remain available. It is not a donor mean, a significance test, or a protein concentration.
  • Named matches link equivalent anatomical names. Related and broader matches are explicitly labeled as such. No sample coordinates have been registered to DKT or BigBrain; no pointwise or layer-specific precision is claimed. Unassigned medial walls receive no expression evidence.
  • The download does not resolve left/right regional expression. The same measurements are used on both hemispheres. Bulk tissue cannot specify which cell expresses a gene. No developmental stage is inferred from this regional map.
  • Below-cutoff and unavailable measurements are distinct. Lack of detection is not proof of biological absence. Reference measurements do not describe a specific person's brain or a disorder.
  • GTEx values provide a separate broad-region RNA check only. Cortical protein immunohistochemistry (IHC) is a separate tissue-level annotation, with its cell type, level, and reliability retained. It cannot verify a DKT parcel. Uncertain staining is labeled uncertain.
  • Some highest measured RNA values occur in cerebellum, white matter, or deep nuclei. Those structures are outside this cortical surface mesh; the protein evidence panel preserves their source names rather than placing them on the cortex.

The article's pathway filters

Filters reproduce nonempty cells of Table 1 in Arnett et al. (2021): Wnt/β-catenin, FMRP, CHD8, and TBR1. Membership may overlap. A blank cell or an unlisted gene does not establish absence of an association. The article has 16 rows; 15 overlap the existing 20-model library. ASXL3 has no supplied model; CNTNAP2, MET, NLGN3, NRXN1, and TBR1 are not table rows.

ST in the table denotes a STRING association score ≥0.30; it is not proof of direct physical binding. Cited reports are distinguished from STRING-only entries. The CHD8 footnote on ADNP, ARID1B, POGZ, KMT5B, and SYNGAP1 reports binding sites without a statistically significant expression fold change. The evidence panel preserves that qualification. These categories are protein networks, not anatomical regions.
